evidence.claim: The UN Geneva summary says the DRC presidency of the Conference on Disarmament planned to hold a plenary focused on cybersecurity in August 2022.
evidence.title: Conference on Disarmament Holds First Public Plenary under the Presidency of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Hears Update from the Coordinators of its Subsidiary Bodies on their Final Reports
evidence.excerpt: The UN Geneva summary says the DRC presidency of the Conference on Disarmament planned to hold a plenary focused on cybersecurity in August 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN meeting summary directly records the DRC-led conference agenda.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional state role under Tshisekedi's administration, not a personal presidential decree.
contrary_evidence: Conference presidency is indirect evidence and does not by itself show national implementation.

evidence.claim: The Ban Monitor profile says the DRC adheres to the core WMD disarmament treaties, is party to a nuclear-weapon-free zone treaty, has no HEU or plutonium stocks, and has no fissile material production.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo
evidence.excerpt: The Ban Monitor profile says the DRC adheres to the core WMD disarmament treaties, is party to a nuclear-weapon-free zone treaty, has no HEU or plutonium stocks, and has no fissile material production.
evidence.source_locator: State profile and key weapons of mass destruction treaties section, lines 29-64 and 88-93
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent technical monitor with treaty and stockpile cross-checks, but the page is a retrospective profile.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective confirmation of a non-nuclear baseline relevant to 2022
evidence.ruler_attribution: State baseline rather than a ruler-specific operational decision.
contrary_evidence: Retrospective profile; use as corroboration, not as the primary legal record.

evidence.claim: The UN Treaty Collection lists the Democratic Republic of the Congo as having ratified the TPNW on 22 September 2022, with entry into force for the DRC on 21 December 2022.
evidence.title: Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons
evidence.excerpt: The UN Treaty Collection lists the Democratic Republic of the Congo as having ratified the TPNW on 22 September 2022, with entry into force for the DRC on 21 December 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Depositary treaty record is authoritative for the ratification date and entry into force.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate-to-high: this was a formal state act under Tshisekedi's government, though executed through foreign-affairs and cabinet channels.
contrary_evidence: This is a legal status record, not proof of deeper implementation beyond ratification.

evidence.claim: ICAN states that the DRC's council of ministers approved TPNW ratification on 6 May 2022 and that President Tshisekedi signed an ordinance on 15 August 2022 authorizing it.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo | Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons
evidence.excerpt: ICAN states that the DRC's council of ministers approved TPNW ratification on 6 May 2022 and that President Tshisekedi signed an ordinance on 15 August 2022 authorizing it.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Secondary source, but the claim is specific and consistent with the UN treaty record on the ratification date.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 process evidence inside the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High for the formal authorization step, because ICAN attributes the ordinance to Tshisekedi personally.
contrary_evidence: The ordinance detail is not independently verified in this pass.

evidence.claim: The IAEA country sheet lists the DRC's NPT safeguards agreement and its additional protocol as in force, and shows the DRC as party to the Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material.
evidence.title: Country List : Office of Legal Affairs : IAEA
evidence.excerpt: The IAEA country sheet lists the DRC's NPT safeguards agreement and its additional protocol as in force, and shows the DRC as party to the Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IAEA status record for safeguards and physical-protection obligations.
evidence.period_fit: Baseline nuclear-safeguards posture in force during 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Low-to-moderate: these are inherited treaty obligations, but they define the non-nuclear baseline under which Tshisekedi governed.
contrary_evidence: This is a standing status record rather than a 2022 policy act by Tshisekedi.

evidence.claim: The council minutes say Tshisekedi validated the 7-pillar National Cybersecurity Strategy, which had been presented on 14 October 2022, and recommended creating a National Cybersecurity Agency and a legal corpus for cybercrime response.
evidence.title: Compte rendu de la soixante-treizième réunion du Conseil des Ministres
evidence.excerpt: The council minutes say Tshisekedi validated the 7-pillar National Cybersecurity Strategy, which had been presented on 14 October 2022, and recommended creating a National Cybersecurity Agency and a legal corpus for cybercrime response.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official minutes show concrete institutional follow-through, though they still record planned implementation rather than finished results.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the minutes explicitly attribute the validation and instructions to Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: This records adoption and recommendation, not actual agency creation or successful execution.

Direct personal-nexus evidence is still sparse: no clear 2022 asset-declaration, campaign-finance, beneficial-ownership, or court/audit record ties Tshisekedi himself to self-dealing or deliberate deception.
Independent, audited delivery and outcome evidence is thinner than the program rhetoric and internal reporting.
